identification_source: Wellmann (ed.) 1906, DMM II 118 (Greek text + RV synonyms: μαλάχη κηπαία, Ῥωμαῖοι μάλβα ὁρτένσε; μαλάχη ἀγρία χερσαία, μάλβα ῥούστικα); Osbaldeston 2000, On Medical Matters, ch. 2-144 (Goodyer numbering): "Malva sylvestris [Linnaeus] — Common Mallow".
excerpt: μολόζη· ἐδωδιμωτέρα ἡ κηπευτὴ μᾶλλον τῆς χερσαίας, κακοστόμαχος δὲ καὶ εὐκοίλιος
notes: Lemma in Wellmann is μολόχη; the First1KGreek digitisation has an OCR error "μολόζη" in the lemma (excerpt copied verbatim incl. the error). The RV synonym list uses μαλάχη. Chapter distinguishes garden (κηπευτή) and wild (χερσαία) mallow; garden mallow of antiquity may not be M. sylvestris s.str. Dimopoulos 2013 p.113: present in all 13 Greek floristic regions, native (no alien status), chorology EA. WCVP: native in Greece, Kriti, East Aegean Is. POWO treats infraspecific taxa (e.g. subsp. mauritiana) as synonyms.

excerpt_edition: Wellmann 1906-1914 (Weidmann, Berlin), public domain; digitised by First1KGreek (Harvard/Leipzig, CC BY-SA 4.0), urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0656.tlg001.1st1K-grc1

alternative_names.name: Cachrys libanotis / Seseli-type umbellifers (the other λιβανωτίδες of Wellmann III 74)

identification_source: Wellmann (ed.) 1906, DMM III 75: "λιβανωτίς, ἣν Ῥωμαῖοι ῤουσμαρῖνον καλοῦσιν, ἧ καὶ οἱ στεφανοπλίκοι χρῶνται" (the libanotis the Romans call rosmarinus, used by garland-makers); Osbaldeston 2000, ch. 3-89: "Rosmarinus officinalis [Linnaeus]".
excerpt: λιβανωτίς, ἣν Ῥωμαῖοι ῤουσμαρῖνον καλοῦσιν, ἧ καὶ οἱ στεφανοπλίκοι χρῶνται· ῥάβδοι εἰσὶ λεπταί
notes: "Libanotis" is ambiguous in DMM: Wellmann III 74 covers umbelliferous libanotides (one fruiting, whose fruit is called κάχρυ), while III 75 is explicitly the plant the Romans call rosmarinus — that chapter is the rosemary one. Basionym/synonym Rosmarinus officinalis L. (synonym in POWO/WCVP). Native status in Greece is partial: Dimopoulos 2013 p.108 lists it in 12 regions with comment (App. III, printed p.~294): "Mostly naturalized from cultivation, but locally native (e.g. in IoI, see also Halácsy 1902: 491)". WCVP: native Greece and East Aegean, introduced on Kriti. Modelling caveat: many Greek GBIF records may be cultivated/naturalised.

evidence.claim: Wellmann III 75 text naming rosmarinus
Salvia rosmarinus Spenn. accepted; Rosmarinus officinalis L. synonym; Lamiaceae; Kriti introduced

identification_source: Wellmann (ed.) 1907, DMM I 75: "ἄρκευθος· ἡ μέν τίς ἐστι μεγάλη ἡ δὲ μικρά" (large and small kinds; RV: Ῥωμαῖοι ζουνιπέρουμ); Osbaldeston 2000 ch. 1-103 suggests Juniperus excelsa and J. communis.
excerpt: ἄρκευθος· ἠ μέν τῖς ἐστι μεγάλη ἡ δὲ μικρά. ἀμφότεραι δὲ θερμαίνουσι καὶ λεπτύνουσι· εἰσὶ δὲ καὶ οὐρητικαί
notes: Two kinds (large/small) are described, so the chapter likely covers more than one Juniperus species; species-level identity not settled by any source I could open. TAXONOMY WARNING: Dimopoulos 2013 (p.42 and App. III) states J. oxycedrus subsp. oxycedrus is a W Mediterranean taxon absent from Greece, replaced by J. oxycedrus subsp. deltoides (R.P.Adams) N.G.Passal.; WCVP/POWO v16 treats J. oxycedrus s.str. as W Mediterranean only (Spain to Italy, N Africa) and accepts Juniperus deltoides R.P.Adams for Greece, Kriti, E Aegean etc. GBIF backbone accepts J. oxycedrus L. (key 2684451). Recommend modelling on GBIF J. oxycedrus key (Greek records = subsp./sp. deltoides) or J. deltoides if separately keyed; J. communis is also native in Greece (Dimopoulos p.42, 9 regions, mountains) and J. macrocarpa coastal.
